gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Techtest.org's bench test found ChatGPT's 'best overall' INIU Carry 45W (P51L-E2) cannot hold 45 W: it dropped to 17 W after about 30 minutes on a laptop and settled around 27 W because of heat, while still delivering 93–98% of its rated capacity. Nor does any result state that the Anker Zolo 20K 30W (A1689) fell to 20 W after about 25% of discharge and went above 70 °C.
standout_why: ChatGPT cited only Best Buy search pages and our page, and the Best Buy pages have no measurements. Of the uncited top results: power-verdict.com says outright that it uses maker spec sheets and Amazon, with no test figures. verdict-reviews.com repeats Macworld's 87% MacBook Pro recharge for the INIU P62-E1 but has no figures for the Carry, the Zolo or the FC11. rosenberryrooms.com has first-person iPhone-charge counts from Arnav Gill (4.5 charges for the INIU 20K 45W built-in cable, 4.2 for the Zolo 30W), a 5-hour Zolo recharge and a claim of '45–50W sustained' for the INIU 65W. It has no Wh capacity, no percentage of rated capacity and no throttling under sustained load. itechguides.com's only measured figure is TechRadar's 85% efficiency for the Anker 737, which is not a candidate. None of them gives a measured sustained output for the 45 W or 30 W built-in-cable banks.
decides: The measurements back the INIU Cougar 65W (P62-E1, $46.99) as the laptop pick, because Macworld recharged a 14-inch M2 MacBook Pro from 0% to 87% with it. They argue against calling the INIU Carry 45W a laptop charger, since Techtest measured it settling around 27 W under laptop load. Our 'Laptop at full speed' cell for the Carry should be phones and tablets only, not 'Small laptops only'. The Carry stays the value pick for phones: its 93–98% measured capacity is the best tested here, against 80–92% for the Anker Zolo 30W. The Zolo's drop to 20 W and readings above 70 °C weaken ChatGPT's 'best Anker option'.
